6. `terraform plan -var="db_password=..." -var="environment=development"` — fix any small drift (add `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [user_data] }` on the launch template if needed).
7. Commit + push.

After the imports succeed and state is in S3, every future plan/apply (local or CI) will see reality and stop trying to recreate things.

## 1. Immediate Commands to Fix Terraform State (Run These NOW)

```powershell
# 1. Clean up the mess
cd "C:\Users\Timothy Kamba\aws-ha-autoscaling-project"

Remove-Item -Recurse -Force aws-ha-autoscaling-project -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Remove-Item -Force terraform\*.tfstate* -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Remove-Item -Force terraform\modules\vpc\*.tfstate* -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

git rm --cached terraform/terraform.tfstate terraform/modules/vpc/terraform.tfstate 2>$null

# 2. Create remote backend (S3 + DynamoDB) — ONE TIME ONLY
$BUCKET = "ha-project-terraform-state-866934333672"
$TABLE  = "ha-project-terraform-locks"

aws s3api create-bucket --bucket $BUCKET --region us-east-1
aws s3api put-bucket-versioning --bucket $BUCKET --versioning-configuration Status=Enabled

aws dynamodb create-table `
  --table-name $TABLE `
  --attribute-definitions AttributeName=LockID,AttributeType=S `
  --key-schema AttributeName=LockID,KeyType=HASH `
  --billing-mode PAY_PER_REQUEST `
  --region us-east-1

# 3. Add the S3 + DynamoDB policy to your GitHub OIDC role (GitHubActionsDeployRole-HAProjectV2)

# 4. Discover your real IDs (very important)
$ALB_VPC = aws elbv2 describe-load-balancers --names ha-project-alb --query "LoadBalancers[0].VpcId" --output text
aws ec2 describe-subnets --filters "Name=vpc-id,Values=$ALB_VPC" --query "Subnets[].[SubnetId, CidrBlock, Tags[?Key=='Name'].Value|[0]]" --output table
```

### 2. Database (PostgreSQL DDL)

Copy and save this as `database/init.sql`:

```sql
-- PostgreSQL Tasks Table for HA To-Do App
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "pgcrypto";

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tasks (
    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    user_id         VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
    title           VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    description     TEXT,
    status          VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' 
                    CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'in_progress', 'completed')),
    priority        VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Medium' 
                    CHECK (priority IN ('Low', 'Medium', 'High')),
    due_date        TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,
    created_at      TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tasks_user_id ON tasks(user_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tasks_status ON tasks(status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tasks_user_status ON tasks(user_id, status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tasks_created_at ON tasks(created_at DESC);

-- Auto-update updated_at
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION update_updated_at_column()
RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
BEGIN
    NEW.updated_at = NOW();
    RETURN NEW;
END;
$$ language 'plpgsql';

DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS update_tasks_updated_at ON tasks;
CREATE TRIGGER update_tasks_updated_at
    BEFORE UPDATE ON tasks
    FOR EACH ROW
    EXECUTE FUNCTION update_updated_at_column();
```

```json
  },
```

**backend/server.js** (full working version)

```javascript
require('dotenv').config();
const express = require('express');
const cors = require('cors');
const { Pool } = require('pg');
const winston = require('winston');
const WinstonCloudWatch = require('winston-cloudwatch');

const app = express();
const PORT = process.env.PORT || 3000;

const logger = winston.createLogger({
  level: 'info',
  format: winston.format.combine(winston.format.timestamp(), winston.format.json()),
  transports: [new winston.transports.Console()]
});

if (process.env.CLOUDWATCH_LOG_GROUP) {
  logger.add(new WinstonCloudWatch({
    logGroupName: process.env.CLOUDWATCH_LOG_GROUP,
    logStreamName: `backend-${new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]}`,
    awsRegion: process.env.AWS_REGION || 'us-east-1',
    jsonMessage: true
  }));
}

const pool = new Pool({
  host: process.env.DB_HOST,
  port: 5432,
  database: process.env.DB_NAME || 'tododb',
  user: process.env.DB_USER,
  password: process.env.DB_PASSWORD,
});

app.use(cors());
app.use(express.json());

app.get('/health', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    await pool.query('SELECT 1');
    res.json({ status: 'healthy', db: 'connected' });
  } catch (e) {
    res.status(503).json({ status: 'unhealthy' });
  }
});

app.get('/api/tasks', async (req, res) => {
  const { userId } = req.query;
  if (!userId) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'userId required' });
  const { rows } = await pool.query(
    'SELECT * FROM tasks WHERE user_id = $1 ORDER BY created_at DESC',
    [userId]
  );
  res.json(rows);
});

app.post('/api/tasks', async (req, res) => {
  const { userId, title, description, priority } = req.body;
  if (!userId || !title) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'userId and title required' });
  const { rows } = await pool.query(
    `INSERT INTO tasks (user_id, title, description, priority) 
     VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4) RETURNING *`,
    [userId, title, description, priority || 'Medium']
  );
  res.status(201).json(rows[0]);
});

app.put('/api/tasks/:id', async (req, res) => {
  const { id } = req.params;
  const { userId, title, description, status, priority } = req.body;
  const { rows } = await pool.query(
    `UPDATE tasks SET 
      title = COALESCE($1, title),
      description = COALESCE($2, description),
      status = COALESCE($3, status),
      priority = COALESCE($4, priority),
      updated_at = NOW()
     WHERE id = $5 AND user_id = $6 RETURNING *`,
    [title, description, status, priority, id, userId]
  );
  if (rows.length === 0) return res.status(404).json({ error: 'Not found' });
  res.json(rows[0]);
});

app.listen(PORT, () => console.log(`Backend running on port ${PORT}`));
```

### Next: Create the Remote Backend (S3 + DynamoDB)

### Block A: Create the S3 bucket + enable versioning

```bash
# Create the bucket (special syntax for us-east-1)
aws s3api create-bucket \
  --bucket ha-project-terraform-state-866934333672 \
  --region us-east-1

# Enable versioning (important for state safety)
aws s3api put-bucket-versioning \
  --bucket ha-project-terraform-state-866934333672 \
  --versioning-configuration Status=Enabled

echo "S3 bucket created successfully"
```

---

### Block B: Create the DynamoDB lock table

```bash
aws dynamodb create-table \
  --table-name ha-project-terraform-locks \
  --attribute-definitions AttributeName=LockID,AttributeType=S \
  --key-schema AttributeName=LockID,KeyType=HASH \
  --billing-mode PAY_PER_REQUEST \
  --region us-east-1

echo "DynamoDB table created"
```

Run this after Block A succeeds.

## Assistant

**Got it.** Let's fix this step by step.

### 1. What is `SecureString`?

`SecureString` is the **encrypted** type in AWS SSM Parameter Store.

- When you store a parameter as `SecureString`, AWS encrypts the value using KMS (Key Management Service).
- When Terraform (or your app) reads it with `with_decryption = true`, it gets the real password in plaintext.
- This is much safer than storing it as a normal `String` type (which is stored in plain text).

This is the recommended type for database passwords, API keys, etc.

---

### 2. Why the command failed

The error `Parameter name must be a fully qualified name` is common in **Git Bash on Windows**. Git Bash sometimes mangles the parameter name.

### Fixed Command (Try this)

Run this version instead (use **single quotes** around the name and value):

```bash
aws ssm put-parameter \
  --name '/ha-project/development/db_password' \
  --value 'Kd929986RDS!' \
  --type SecureString \
  --overwrite
```

If it still fails, run it in **PowerShell** instead (recommended for this command):

```powershell
aws ssm put-parameter `
  --name '/ha-project/development/db_password' `
  --value 'Kd929986RDS!' `
  --type SecureString `
  --overwrite
```

---

### Why it failed in Git Bash but worked in PowerShell

This is very common on Windows:

- **Git Bash** uses a Unix-like environment (MinGW/MSYS). It has different quoting and line-continuation rules. When you use `\` for line continuation + quotes around values, the AWS CLI (which is a Windows Python program) often receives mangled arguments.
- **PowerShell** (and Command Prompt) use Windows-native argument parsing, so the AWS CLI receives the parameters cleanly.

**Rule of thumb**: For AWS CLI commands that involve quotes, JSON, or SecureString parameters, **PowerShell is usually more reliable** on Windows than Git Bash.

### Answers to Your Two Questions

**1. "can just right click to paste in PowerShell?"**

Yes, in most cases:

- In **Windows Terminal** (recommended) → Right-click usually pastes.
- In the old PowerShell window → You may need to enable **QuickEdit Mode** (right-click title bar → Properties → Options → check QuickEdit Mode).
- Best modern way: Use **Ctrl + Shift + V** (works in Windows Terminal).

**2. Are Bash and PowerShell used interchangeably as a cloud/devops professional?**

Not really. Here's the honest reality in the industry:

| Situation                        | Preferred Shell          | Why |
|----------------------------------|--------------------------|-----|
| Local development on **Linux/Mac** | Bash / Zsh              | Native and excellent |
| Local development on **Windows**   | **PowerShell 7+**       | Much better argument handling with AWS CLI, Azure CLI, Terraform, etc. |
| CI/CD pipelines                  | Bash (usually)          | Most runners (GitHub, GitLab, etc.) are Linux-based |
| Scripting & automation           | PowerShell (on Windows) or Python | PowerShell is a first-class language now |
| Troubleshooting / Debugging      | Whatever works fastest  | Many people use both |

**Real talk from the field:**
- Most serious Windows-based DevOps/SRE/Cloud engineers have moved to **PowerShell 7** for day-to-day AWS/Azure work.
- Git Bash is still used, but a lot of people treat it as "good enough for git" rather than their primary shell for cloud tooling.
- You will see both in the wild, but PowerShell tends to cause fewer weird quoting/escaping bugs with the AWS CLI on Windows.

### Fix 1: RDS Security Group (Stop the Destroy)

Replace the current `aws_security_group.rds_sg` block in `terraform/rds.tf` with this version:

```hcl
resource "aws_security_group" "rds_sg" {
  name        = "rds-security-group"
  description = "Allow MySQL from EC2 instances"
  vpc_id      = module.vpc.vpc_id   # This will now resolve correctly after the VPC import

  ingress {
```

### Fix 2: Launch Template (Prevent User Data Replacement)

In `terraform/modules/ec2/main.tf`, inside the `aws_launch_template.lt` resource, add this block at the bottom (before the closing `}`):

```hcl
lifecycle {
```

This is the standard safe pattern when you don’t want Terraform to force new instances every time the user-data string changes.

**`http://ha-project-alb-1568483483.us-east-1.elb.amazonaws.com`**

Here’s the updated version you can copy-paste:

```tsx
import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';

const API_BASE = 'http://ha-project-alb-1568483483.us-east-1.elb.amazonaws.com/api';

interface Todo {
  id: string;
  task: string;
  status?: string;
  priority?: string;
}

const TodoApp: React.FC = () => {
  const [user, setUser] = useState<any>(null);
  const [todos, setTodos] = useState<Todo[]>([]);
  const [newTodo, setNewTodo] = useState('');
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);

  const userId = user?.uid || 'demo-user-123';

  const fetchTodos = async () => {
    try {
      setLoading(true);
      const res = await fetch(`${API_BASE}/tasks?userId=${userId}`);
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error('API error');
      const data = await res.json();
      setTodos(data.map((t: any) => ({
        id: t.id,
        task: t.task || t.title,
        status: t.status,
        priority: t.priority
      })));
    } catch (e) {
      console.error('Failed to fetch tasks', e);
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  };

  const addTodo = async () => {
    if (!newTodo.trim()) return;
    try {
      await fetch(`${API_BASE}/tasks`, {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify({
          userId,
          title: newTodo.trim(),
          priority: 'Medium'
        })
      });
      setNewTodo('');
      await fetchTodos();
    } catch (e) {
      alert('Failed to save task. Is the backend running?');
    }
  };

  const toggleComplete = async (todo: Todo) => {
    const newStatus = todo.status === 'completed' ? 'pending' : 'completed';
    try {
      await fetch(`${API_BASE}/tasks/${todo.id}`, {
        method: 'PUT',
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify({ userId, status: newStatus })
      });
      await fetchTodos();
    } catch (e) {
      alert('Update failed');
    }
  };

  useEffect(() => {
    const saved = localStorage.getItem('user');
    if (saved) {
      const u = JSON.parse(saved);
      setUser(u);
    }
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (user) fetchTodos();
  }, [user]);

  return (
    <div style={{ padding: '30px', maxWidth: '720px', margin: '0 auto', fontFamily: 'system-ui' }}>
      <h1>✅ HA To-Do — Persisted in RDS (MySQL)</h1>
      <p style={{ color: '#666', fontSize: '14px' }}>API: {API_BASE}</p>

      {!user ? (
        <button
          onClick={() => {
            const mock = { uid: 'demo-user-123', displayName: 'Demo User' };
            setUser(mock);
```

### 1. Backend → Switched to MySQL (`mysql2`)

Here's the updated `backend/server.js` that works with your existing MySQL database (`myapp-rds`):

```js
require('dotenv').config();
const express = require('express');
const cors = require('cors');
const mysql = require('mysql2/promise');
const winston = require('winston');

const app = express();
const PORT = process.env.PORT || 3000;

const logger = winston.createLogger({
  level: process.env.LOG_LEVEL || 'info',
  format: winston.format.combine(
    winston.format.timestamp(),
    winston.format.json()
  ),
  transports: [new winston.transports.Console()]
});

const pool = mysql.createPool({
  host: process.env.DB_HOST,
  user: process.env.DB_USER,
  password: process.env.DB_PASSWORD,
  database: 'myappdb',
  waitForConnections: true,
  connectionLimit: 10,
  queueLimit: 0
});

app.use(cors());
app.use(express.json());

app.get('/health', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    await pool.query('SELECT 1');
    res.json({ status: 'healthy', db: 'connected' });
  } catch (e) {
    res.status(503).json({ status: 'unhealthy' });
  }
});

app.get('/api/tasks', async (req, res) => {
  const { userId } = req.query;
  if (!userId) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'userId required' });

  try {
    const [rows] = await pool.query(
      'SELECT * FROM tasks WHERE user_id = ? ORDER BY created_at DESC',
      [userId]
    );
    res.json(rows);
  } catch (e) {
    logger.error('Failed to fetch tasks', { error: e.message });
    res.status(500).json({ error: 'Failed to fetch tasks' });
  }
});

app.post('/api/tasks', async (req, res) => {
  const { userId, title, description, priority } = req.body;
  if (!userId || !title) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'userId and title required' });

  try {
    const [result] = await pool.query(
      'INSERT INTO tasks (user_id, task, description, priority) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)',
      [userId, title, description || null, priority || 'Medium']
    );
    res.status(201).json({ id: result.insertId, userId, task: title, status: 'pending' });
  } catch (e) {
    logger.error('Failed to create task', { error: e.message });
    res.status(500).json({ error: 'Failed to create task' });
  }
});

app.put('/api/tasks/:id', async (req, res) => {
  const { id } = req.params;
  const { userId, title, description, status, priority } = req.body;

  try {
    const fields = [];
    const values = [];

    if (title !== undefined) { fields.push('task = ?'); values.push(title); }
    if (description !== undefined) { fields.push('description = ?'); values.push(description); }
    if (status !== undefined) { fields.push('status = ?'); values.push(status); }
    if (priority !== undefined) { fields.push('priority = ?'); values.push(priority); }

    if (fields.length === 0) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'No fields to update' });

    values.push(id, userId);

    const [result] = await pool.query(
      `UPDATE tasks SET ${fields.join(', ')} WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ?`,
      values
    );

    if (result.affectedRows === 0) return res.status(404).json({ error: 'Task not found' });
    res.json({ success: true });
  } catch (e) {
    logger.error('Failed to update task', { error: e.message });
    res.status(500).json({ error: 'Failed to update task' });
  }
});

app.listen(PORT, '0.0.0.0', () => {
  logger.info(`Backend running on port ${PORT}`);
});
```

```tsx
import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';

const API_BASE = 'http://ha-project-alb-1568483483.us-east-1.elb.amazonaws.com/api';

interface Todo {
  id: string;
  task: string;
  status?: string;
  priority?: string;
}

const TodoApp: React.FC = () => {
  const [user, setUser] = useState<any>(null);
  const [todos, setTodos] = useState<Todo[]>([]);
  const [newTodo, setNewTodo] = useState('');
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);

  const userId = user?.uid || 'demo-user-123';

  const fetchTodos = async () => {
    try {
      setLoading(true);
      const res = await fetch(`${API_BASE}/tasks?userId=${userId}`);
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error('API error');
      const data = await res.json();
      setTodos(data.map((t: any) => ({
        id: t.id,
        task: t.task || t.title,
        status: t.status,
        priority: t.priority
      })));
    } catch (e) {
      console.error('Failed to fetch tasks', e);
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  };

  const addTodo = async () => {
    if (!newTodo.trim()) return;
    try {
      await fetch(`${API_BASE}/tasks`, {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify({ userId, title: newTodo.trim(), priority: 'Medium' })
      });
      setNewTodo('');
      await fetchTodos();
    } catch {
      alert('Failed to save task');
    }
  };

  const toggleComplete = async (todo: Todo) => {
    const newStatus = todo.status === 'completed' ? 'pending' : 'completed';
    try {
      await fetch(`${API_BASE}/tasks/${todo.id}`, {
        method: 'PUT',
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify({ userId, status: newStatus })
      });
      await fetchTodos();
    } catch {
      alert('Update failed');
    }
  };

  useEffect(() => {
    const saved = localStorage.getItem('user');
    if (saved) setUser(JSON.parse(saved));
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (user) fetchTodos();
  }, [user]);

  return (
    <div style={{
      minHeight: '100vh',
      background: 'linear-gradient(135deg, #f5f7fa 0%, #e4e8ec 100%)',
      padding: '40px 20px',
      fontFamily: 'system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif'
    }}>
      <div style={{ maxWidth: '680px', margin: '0 auto' }}>
        <h1 style={{ 
          fontSize: '42px', 
          fontWeight: 700, 
          textAlign: 'center', 
          marginBottom: '8px',
          color: '#1a1a1a'
        }}>
          To <span style={{ color: '#666', fontWeight: 400 }}>·</span> Do
        </h1>
        <p style={{ textAlign: 'center', color: '#666', marginBottom: '32px' }}>
          Persisted in MySQL RDS
        </p>

        {!user ? (
          <div style={{ textAlign: 'center' }}>
            <button 
              onClick={() => {
                const mock = { uid: 'demo-user-123', displayName: 'Demo User' };
                setUser(mock);
                localStorage.setItem('user', JSON.stringify(mock));
              }}
              style={{
                padding: '14px 32px',
                fontSize: 18,
                background: '#000',
                color: 'white',
                border: 'none',
                borderRadius: 8,
                cursor: 'pointer'
              }}
            >
              Sign in to start
            </button>
          </div>
        ) : (
          <div style={{
            background: 'white',
            borderRadius: 16,
            boxShadow: '0 10px 30px rgba(0,0,0,0.08)',
            padding: '32px'
          }}>
            <p style={{ marginBottom: 24, color: '#444' }}>
              Welcome, <strong>{user.displayName}</strong>
            </p>

            <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 12, marginBottom: 28 }}>
              <input
                value={newTodo}
                onChange={e => setNewTodo(e.target.value)}
                placeholder="What needs to be done?"
                style={{
                  flex: 1,
                  padding: '14px 18px',
                  fontSize: 16,
                  border: '1px solid #ddd',
                  borderRadius: 10,
                  outline: 'none'
                }}
                onKeyDown={e => e.key === 'Enter' && addTodo()}
              />
              <button 
                onClick={addTodo} 
                disabled={loading}
                style={{
                  padding: '14px 28px',
                  background: '#000',
                  color: 'white',
                  border: 'none',
                  borderRadius: 10,
                  fontSize: 15,
                  cursor: 'pointer'
                }}
              >
                Add
              </button>
            </div>

            {loading && <p style={{ color: '#888' }}>Loading...</p>}

            <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: 10 }}>
              {todos.length === 0 && !loading && (
                <p style={{ color: '#999', textAlign: 'center', padding: '20px 0' }}>
                  No tasks yet. Add one above!
                </p>
              )}

              {todos.map(todo => (
                <div 
                  key={todo.id}
                  style={{
                    display: 'flex',
                    alignItems: 'center',
                    gap: 14,
                    padding: '16px 20px',
                    background: '#fafafa',
                    borderRadius: 12,
                    border: '1px solid #eee'
                  }}
                >
                  <input
                    type="checkbox"

                    style={{ width: 20, height: 20, cursor: 'pointer' }}
                  />
                  <span style={{ 
                    flex: 1, 
                    fontSize: 16,
                    textDecoration: todo.status === 'completed' ? 'line-through' : 'none',
                    color: todo.status === 'completed' ? '#888' : '#222'
                  }}>
                    {todo.task}
                  </span>
                  {todo.priority && (
                    <span style={{
                      fontSize: 12,

                      color: '#555'
                    }}>
                      {todo.priority}
                    </span>
                  )}
                </div>
              ))}
            </div>

            <div style={{ marginTop: 32, textAlign: 'center' }}>
              <button 
                onClick={() => { localStorage.removeItem('user'); window.location.reload(); }}
                style={{ color: '#666', background: 'none', border: 'none', cursor: 'pointer' }}
              >
                Sign out
              </button>
            </div>
          </div>
        )}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
};

export default TodoApp;
```

| Resource | Purpose | Why It Matters for SAA |
|---------|--------|------------------------|
| **CloudWatch Log Group** (`/aws/ec2/ha-project-backend`) | Central place where your Node.js backend logs will go | Observability + centralized logging (SAA topic) |
| **CloudWatch Log Stream** | Individual stream inside the Log Group (one per day/environment) | Helps you search logs by date |
| **RDS CPU Alarm** | Triggers if CPU > 80% for 10 minutes | Proactive monitoring + Auto Scaling triggers |
| **RDS Free Storage Alarm** | Triggers if free storage < 5GB | Prevents your database from running out of space |

#### Option B – More complete (better long-term)
Give the role broader IAM read permissions (many people doing Terraform + GitHub OIDC do this temporarily):

```json

    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Action": [
        "iam:GetRole",
        "iam:GetRolePolicy",
        "iam:ListRolePolicies",
```

**Full corrected `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`:**

```yaml
name: CI/CD - HA 3-Tier To-Do App (React + Node + MySQL)

on:
  push:
    branches: [development, staging, main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  id-token: write
  contents: read

env:
  AWS_REGION: us-east-1
  TF_STATE_BUCKET: ha-project-terraform-state-866934333672
  TF_LOCK_TABLE: ha-project-terraform-locks
  FRONTEND_BUCKET: ha-project-frontend-builds
  OIDC_ROLE: arn:aws:iam::866934333672:role/GitHubActionsDeployRole-HAProjectV2

jobs:
  # ===================== BUILD =====================
  build:
    name: Build React + Backend
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: 'npm'
          cache-dependency-path: |
            app/package-lock.json
            backend/package-lock.json

      - name: Build React Frontend
        working-directory: ./app
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm run build

      - name: Package Backend (self-contained with dependencies)
        working-directory: ./backend
        run: |
          npm ci --omit=dev
          zip -r ../backend.zip .

      - name: Upload Frontend Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: react-build
          path: app/build

      - name: Upload Backend Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: backend-zip
          path: backend.zip

  # ===================== TEST + TERRAFORM PLAN =====================
  test-plan:
    name: Test & Terraform Plan
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Configure AWS via OIDC
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ env.OIDC_ROLE }}
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: "~> 1.7"

      - name: Terraform Init (Remote Backend)
        working-directory: ./terraform
        run: |
          terraform init \
            -backend-config="bucket=${{ env.TF_STATE_BUCKET }}" \
            -backend-config="key=ha-project/${{ github.ref_name }}/terraform.tfstate" \
            -backend-config="region=${{ env.AWS_REGION }}" \
            -backend-config="dynamodb_table=${{ env.TF_LOCK_TABLE }}" \
            -backend-config="encrypt=true" \
            -reconfigure

      - name: Terraform Validate
        working-directory: ./terraform
        run: terraform validate

      - name: Terraform Plan
        working-directory: ./terraform
        run: |
          terraform plan \
            -refresh=false \
            -var="db_password=${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}" \
            -var="environment=${{ github.ref_name == 'main' && 'production' || github.ref_name == 'staging' && 'staging' || 'development' }}" \
            -out=tfplan

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: tfplan-${{ github.ref_name }}
          path: terraform/tfplan

  # ===================== DEPLOY TO DEVELOPMENT (AUTO) =====================
  deploy-dev:
    name: Deploy to Development
    needs: [build, test-plan]
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/development'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Configure AWS via OIDC
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ env.OIDC_ROLE }}
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3

      - name: Terraform Init
        working-directory: ./terraform
        run: |
          terraform init \
            -backend-config="bucket=${{ env.TF_STATE_BUCKET }}" \
            -backend-config="key=ha-project/development/terraform.tfstate" \
            -backend-config="region=${{ env.AWS_REGION }}" \
            -backend-config="use_lockfile=true" \
            -backend-config="encrypt=true"

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: tfplan-development
          path: terraform/

      - name: Targeted Foundational Apply (S3 + IAM + CloudWatch - safe during drift repair)
        working-directory: ./terraform
        run: |
          terraform apply \
            -refresh=false \
            -var="db_password=${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}" \
            -var="environment=development" \
            -target=aws_s3_bucket.frontend_builds \
            -target=aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block.frontend_builds \
            -target=aws_s3_bucket_versioning.frontend_builds \
            -target=module.ec2.aws_iam_role.ec2_role \
            -target=module.ec2.aws_iam_role_policy.s3_frontend_read \
            -target=module.ec2.aws_iam_instance_profile.ec2_profile \
            -target=module.monitoring \
            -auto-approve || true

      - name: Full Terraform Apply (Development)
        working-directory: ./terraform
        run: |
          terraform apply \
            -refresh=false \
```

```yaml
          cache: 'npm'

            backend/package-lock.json

      - name: Build React Frontend
        working-directory: ./app
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm run build

      - name: Package Backend (self-contained with dependencies)

        run: |
          npm ci --omit=dev

      - name: Upload Frontend Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: react-build
          path: app/build

      - name: Upload Backend Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:

          path: backend.zip

  # ===================== TEST + TERRAFORM PLAN =====================

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4

  deploy-dev:
```

## Assistant

**This is a known (and annoying) Terraform S3 backend + DynamoDB locking corruption issue.**

### What the error actually means
Terraform stores your state file in S3, and it used to also keep a "checksum/digest" record in DynamoDB (the old locking method). The two got out of sync — this commonly happens after interrupted applies, backend config changes, or when switching between `dynamodb_table` and `use_lockfile=true`.

Right now Terraform refuses to proceed because it thinks someone (or something) tampered with the state.

---

### Fastest way to unblock you (for the demo)

You have two practical options right now:

### Option A — Best (Recommended)
Manually fix the stale lock record in DynamoDB:

1. Go to the AWS Console → **DynamoDB** → Tables → `ha-project-terraform-locks`
2. Click on the table → **Explore table items**
3. Search for the item where the key/partition is something like:
   - `LockID` = `ha-project-terraform-state-866934333672/ha-project/development/terraform.tfstate`
4. **Delete** that item (or edit it and set the `Digest` field to the value Terraform gave you):
   ```
   a25cfd8196fb59ddc43852c1bbf3a170
   ```
5. Wait 10–20 seconds, then re-trigger the workflow on `development`.

This is the cleanest fix.

---

### Option B — Emergency workaround (if you can't touch DynamoDB right now)
We can temporarily tell Terraform in the **test-plan** job to skip locking entirely.

```yaml
  # ===================== BUILD =====================
  build:
    name: Build React + Backend
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: 'npm'
          cache-dependency-path: |
            app/package-lock.json
            backend/package-lock.json

      - name: Build React Frontend
        working-directory: ./app
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm run build

      - name: Package Backend (self-contained with dependencies)
        working-directory: ./backend
        run: |
          npm ci --omit=dev
          zip -r ../backend.zip .

      - name: Upload Frontend Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: react-build
          path: app/build

      - name: Upload Backend Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: backend-zip
          path: backend.zip

  # ===================== TEST + TERRAFORM PLAN =====================
  test-plan:
    name: Test & Terraform Plan
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Configure AWS via OIDC
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ env.OIDC_ROLE }}
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: "~> 1.7"

      - name: Terraform Init (Remote Backend)
        working-directory: ./terraform
        run: |
          terraform init \
            -backend-config="bucket=${{ env.TF_STATE_BUCKET }}" \
            -backend-config="key=ha-project/${{ github.ref_name }}/terraform.tfstate" \
            -backend-config="region=${{ env.AWS_REGION }}" \
            -backend-config="use_lockfile=true" \
            -backend-config="encrypt=true" \
            -reconfigure

      - name: Terraform Validate
        working-directory: ./terraform
        run: terraform validate

      - name: Terraform Plan
        working-directory: ./terraform
        run: |
          terraform plan \
            -refresh=false \
            -lock=false \
            -var="db_password=${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}" \
            -var="environment=${{ github.ref_name == 'main' && 'production' || github.ref_name == 'staging' && 'staging' || 'development' }}" \
            -out=tfplan

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: tfplan-${{ github.ref_name }}
          path: terraform/tfplan

  # ===================== DEPLOY TO DEVELOPMENT (AUTO) =====================
  deploy-dev:
    name: Deploy to Development
    needs: [build, test-plan]
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/development'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Configure AWS via OIDC
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ env.OIDC_ROLE }}
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3

      - name: Terraform Init
        working-directory: ./terraform
        run: |
          terraform init \
            -backend-config="bucket=${{ env.TF_STATE_BUCKET }}" \
            -backend-config="key=ha-project/development/terraform.tfstate" \
            -backend-config="region=${{ env.AWS_REGION }}" \
            -backend-config="use_lockfile=true" \
            -backend-config="encrypt=true"

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: tfplan-development
          path: terraform/

      - name: Targeted Foundational Apply (S3 + IAM + CloudWatch - safe during drift repair)
        working-directory: ./terraform
        run: |
          terraform apply \
            -refresh=false \
            -lock=false \
            -var="db_password=${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}" \
            -var="environment=development" \
            -target=aws_s3_bucket.frontend_builds \
            -target=aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block.frontend_builds \
            -target=aws_s3_bucket_versioning.frontend_builds \
            -target=module.ec2.aws_iam_role.ec2_role \
            -target=module.ec2.aws_iam_role_policy.s3_frontend_read \
            -target=module.ec2.aws_iam_instance_profile.ec2_profile \
            -target=module.monitoring \
            -auto-approve || true

      - name: Full Terraform Apply (Development)
        working-directory: ./terraform
        run: |
          terraform apply \
            -refresh=false \
            -lock=false \
            -var="db_password=${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}" \
            -var="environment=development" \
            -auto-approve

      - name: Download React Build Artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: react-build
          path: app/build

      - name: Download Backend Artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: backend-zip
          path: .

      - name: Deploy React + Backend to S3
        run: |
          # Frontend
          aws s3 sync ./app/build s3://${{ env.FRONTEND_BUCKET }}/frontend/current/ --delete
          # Backend (now self-contained with node_modules from the build job)
          aws s3 cp backend.zip s3://${{ env.FRONTEND_BUCKET }}/backend/backend.zip

      - name: Trigger ASG Refresh (pick up new code)
        run: |
          aws autoscaling start-instance-refresh \
            --auto-scaling-group-name ha-project-asg \
            --strategy Rolling \
            --preferences MinHealthyPercentage=50,InstanceWarmup=180 \
            --region ${{ env.AWS_REGION }} || echo "Refresh skipped"

  # ===================== DEPLOY TO STAGING (AUTO after dev) =====================
  deploy-staging:
    name: Deploy to Staging
    needs: deploy-dev
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/staging'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Configure AWS via OIDC
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ env.OIDC_ROLE }}
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3

      - name: Terraform Init (Staging State)
        working-directory: ./terraform
        run: |
          terraform init \
            -backend-config="bucket=${{ env.TF_STATE_BUCKET }}" \
            -backend-config="key=ha-project/staging/terraform.tfstate" \
            -backend-config="region=${{ env.AWS_REGION }}" \
            -backend-config="use_lockfile=true" \
            -backend-config="encrypt=true"

      - name: Apply to Staging
        working-directory: ./terraform
        run: |
          terraform apply \
            -refresh=false \
            -lock=false \
            -var="db_password=${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}" \
            -var="environment=staging" \
            -auto-approve

      - name: Download React Build Artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: react-build
          path: app/build

      - name: Download Backend Artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: backend-zip
          path: .

      - name: Deploy artifacts to Staging S3 prefix (extend later)
        run: |
          aws s3 sync ./app/build s3://${{ env.FRONTEND_BUCKET }}/frontend/staging/ --delete || true
          # Backend upload for staging is commented out for now (extend later)
          # aws s3 cp backend.zip s3://${{ env.FRONTEND_BUCKET }}/backend/backend-staging.zip || true

  # ===================== PRODUCTION (MANUAL APPROVAL GATE) =====================
  #
  # MANUAL APPROVAL FLOW EXPLANATION:
  # - When code is pushed to the 'main' branch, the pipeline runs through build + test-plan.
  # - It then reaches the 'deploy-prod-approval' job.
  # - This job uses GitHub Environments (environment: production).
  # - Because of this, GitHub will pause the workflow and require manual approval
  #   before continuing to the actual 'deploy-prod' job.
  # - Approvers can approve (or reject) directly in the GitHub UI under the run's
  #   "Review deployments" section.
  # - This is the standard, secure way to gate production deployments.
  # - The placeholder URL below can be updated later once you have a custom domain.
  #
  deploy-prod-approval:
    name: Production Approval Gate
    needs: [build, test-plan]
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: production
      url: https://github.com  # Replace with your prod ALB DNS later
    steps:
      - run: echo "✅ Manual approval granted for Production deployment"

  deploy-prod:
    name: Deploy to Production
    needs: deploy-prod-approval
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Configure AWS via OIDC
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ env.OIDC_ROLE }}
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3

      - name: Terraform Init (Prod State)
        working-directory: ./terraform
        run: |
          terraform init \
            -backend-config="bucket=${{ env.TF_STATE_BUCKET }}" \
            -backend-config="key=ha-project/production/terraform.tfstate" \
            -backend-config="region=${{ env.AWS_REGION }}" \
            -backend-config="use_lockfile=true" \
            -backend-config="encrypt=true"

      - name: Production Apply (with extra caution)
        working-directory: ./terraform
        run: |
          terraform apply \
            -refresh=false \
            -lock=false \
            -var="db_password=${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}" \
            -var="environment=production" \
            -auto-approve

      - name: Download React Build Artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: react-build
          path: app/build

      - name: Download Backend Artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: backend-zip
          path: .

      - name: Deploy to Production S3
        run: |
          aws s3 sync ./app/build s3://${{ env.FRONTEND_BUCKET }}/frontend/production/ --delete || true
          aws s3 cp backend.zip s3://${{ env.FRONTEND_BUCKET }}/backend/backend-prod.zip
```

## Assistant

**Got it — this is the exact reason it broke.**

### What happened

You were making progress because the **test-plan** job was still using the old backend config style (`dynamodb_table`).

When we updated the test-plan job to use the modern `use_lockfile=true` (to fix the previous S3/DynamoDB checksum error), we left the Terraform version pinned at `~> 1.7`.

`use_lockfile` is a **Terraform 1.10+** feature. Version 1.7 doesn't know what that argument is, so `terraform init` now fails with:

> `Invalid backend configuration argument: "use_lockfile" ... is not expected`

This is why it "was working before" and "went backwards" after the recent change.

---

### Fix (very small)

In your local `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, find this block in the **Test & Terraform Plan** job:

```yaml
      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: "~> 1.7"
```

**Change it to:**

```yaml
      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: "~> 1.10"
```

Then run:

```bash
git add .github/workflows/deploy.yml
git commit -m "fix: bump Terraform version to 1.10+ to support use_lockfile backend"
git push origin development
```

After pushing, re-trigger the pipeline on `development`.

### Full updated `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`

```yaml
name: CI/CD - HA 3-Tier To-Do App (React + Node + MySQL)

on:
  push:
    branches: [development, staging, main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  id-token: write
  contents: read

env:
  AWS_REGION: us-east-1
  TF_STATE_BUCKET: ha-project-terraform-state-866934333672
  TF_LOCK_TABLE: ha-project-terraform-locks
  FRONTEND_BUCKET: ha-project-frontend-builds
  OIDC_ROLE: arn:aws:iam::866934333672:role/GitHubActionsDeployRole-HAProjectV2

jobs:
  # ===================== BUILD =====================
  build:
    name: Build React + Backend
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: 'npm'
          cache-dependency-path: |
            app/package-lock.json
            backend/package-lock.json

      - name: Build React Frontend
        working-directory: ./app
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm run build

      - name: Package Backend (self-contained with dependencies)
        working-directory: ./backend
        run: |
          npm ci --omit=dev
          zip -r ../backend.zip .

      - name: Upload Frontend Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: react-build
          path: app/build

      - name: Upload Backend Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: backend-zip
          path: backend.zip

  # ===================== TEST + TERRAFORM PLAN =====================
  test-plan:
    name: Test & Terraform Plan
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Configure AWS via OIDC
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ env.OIDC_ROLE }}
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: "~> 1.10"

      - name: Terraform Init (Remote Backend)
        working-directory: ./terraform
        run: |
          terraform init \
            -backend-config="bucket=${{ env.TF_STATE_BUCKET }}" \
            -backend-config="key=ha-project/${{ github.ref_name }}/terraform.tfstate" \
            -backend-config="region=${{ env.AWS_REGION }}" \
            -backend-config="use_lockfile=true" \
            -backend-config="encrypt=true" \
            -reconfigure

      - name: Terraform Validate
        working-directory: ./terraform
        run: terraform validate

      - name: Terraform Plan
        working-directory: ./terraform
        run: |
          terraform plan \
            -refresh=false \
            -lock=false \
            -var="db_password=${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}" \
            -var="environment=${{ github.ref_name == 'main' && 'production' || github.ref_name == 'staging' && 'staging' || 'development' }}" \
            -out=tfplan

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: tfplan-${{ github.ref_name }}
          path: terraform/tfplan

  # ===================== DEPLOY TO DEVELOPMENT (AUTO) =====================
  deploy-dev:
    name: Deploy to Development
    needs: [build, test-plan]
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/development'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Configure AWS via OIDC
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ env.OIDC_ROLE }}
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3

      - name: Terraform Init
        working-directory: ./terraform
        run: |
          terraform init \
            -backend-config="bucket=${{ env.TF_STATE_BUCKET }}" \
            -backend-config="key=ha-project/development/terraform.tfstate" \
            -backend-config="region=${{ env.AWS_REGION }}" \
            -backend-config="use_lockfile=true" \
            -backend-config="encrypt=true"

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: tfplan-development
          path: terraform/

      - name: Targeted Foundational Apply (S3 + IAM + CloudWatch - safe during drift repair)
        working-directory: ./terraform
        run: |
          terraform apply \
            -refresh=false \
            -lock=false \
            -var="db_password=${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}" \
            -var="environment=development" \
            -target=aws_s3_bucket.frontend_builds \
            -target=aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block.frontend_builds \
            -target=aws_s3_bucket_versioning.frontend_builds \
            -target=module.ec2.aws_iam_role.ec2_role \
            -target=module.ec2.aws_iam_role_policy.s3_frontend_read \
            -target=module.ec2.aws_iam_instance_profile.ec2_profile \
            -target=module.monitoring \
            -auto-approve || true

      - name: Full Terraform Apply (Development)
        working-directory: ./terraform
        run: |
          terraform apply \
            -refresh=false \
            -lock=false \
            -var="db_password=${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}" \
            -var="environment=development" \
            -auto-approve

      - name: Download React Build Artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: react-build
          path: app/build

      - name: Download Backend Artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: backend-zip
          path: .

      - name: Deploy React + Backend to S3
        run: |
          # Frontend
          aws s3 sync ./app/build s3://${{ env.FRONTEND_BUCKET }}/frontend/current/ --delete
          # Backend (now self-contained with node_modules from the build job)
          aws s3 cp backend.zip s3://${{ env.FRONTEND_BUCKET }}/backend/backend.zip

      - name: Trigger ASG Refresh (pick up new code)
        run: |
          aws autoscaling start-instance-refresh \
            --auto-scaling-group-name ha-project-asg \
            --strategy Rolling \
            --preferences MinHealthyPercentage=50,InstanceWarmup=180 \
            --region ${{ env.AWS_REGION }} || echo "Refresh skipped"

  # ===================== DEPLOY TO STAGING (AUTO after dev) =====================
  deploy-staging:
    name: Deploy to Staging
    needs: deploy-dev
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/staging'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Configure AWS via OIDC
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ env.OIDC_ROLE }}
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3

      - name: Terraform Init (Staging State)
        working-directory: ./terraform
        run: |
          terraform init \
            -backend-config="bucket=${{ env.TF_STATE_BUCKET }}" \
            -backend-config="key=ha-project/staging/terraform.tfstate" \
            -backend-config="region=${{ env.AWS_REGION }}" \
            -backend-config="use_lockfile=true" \
            -backend-config="encrypt=true"

      - name: Apply to Staging
        working-directory: ./terraform
        run: |
          terraform apply \
            -refresh=false \
            -lock=false \
            -var="db_password=${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}" \
            -var="environment=staging" \
            -auto-approve

      - name: Download React Build Artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: react-build
          path: app/build

      - name: Download Backend Artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: backend-zip
          path: .

      - name: Deploy artifacts to Staging S3 prefix (extend later)
        run: |
          aws s3 sync ./app/build s3://${{ env.FRONTEND_BUCKET }}/frontend/staging/ --delete || true
          # Backend upload for staging is commented out for now (extend later)
          # aws s3 cp backend.zip s3://${{ env.FRONTEND_BUCKET }}/backend/backend-staging.zip || true

  # ===================== PRODUCTION (MANUAL APPROVAL GATE) =====================
  #
  # PROMOTION FLOW:
  #   Push to development branch → Deploy to Development
  #   Push to staging branch     → Deploy to Staging
  #   Push to main branch        → Approve Production Deployment (manual gate) → Deploy to Production
  #
  # The approval job depends on deploy-staging so the Actions graph shows a clear chain:
  # Test & Terraform Plan → Deploy to Staging → Approve Production Deployment → Deploy to Production
  #
  # MANUAL APPROVAL:
  # - Uses the "production" GitHub Environment (configure required reviewers in repo settings).
  # - Approvers approve/reject from the "Review deployments" section in the run.
  # - Update the environment URL to your real prod ALB DNS later.
  #
  deploy-prod-approval:
    name: Approve Production Deployment
    needs: [build, test-plan, deploy-staging]
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: production
      url: https://github.com  # Replace with your prod ALB DNS later
    steps:
      - run: echo "✅ Manual approval granted for Production deployment"

  deploy-prod:
    name: Deploy to Production
    needs: deploy-prod-approval
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Configure AWS via OIDC
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ env.OIDC_ROLE }}
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3

      - name: Terraform Init (Prod State)
        working-directory: ./terraform
        run: |
          terraform init \
            -backend-config="bucket=${{ env.TF_STATE_BUCKET }}" \
            -backend-config="key=ha-project/production/terraform.tfstate" \
            -backend-config="region=${{ env.AWS_REGION }}" \
            -backend-config="use_lockfile=true" \
            -backend-config="encrypt=true"

      - name: Production Apply (with extra caution)
        working-directory: ./terraform
        run: |
          terraform apply \
            -refresh=false \
            -lock=false \
            -var="db_password=${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}" \
            -var="environment=production" \
            -auto-approve

      - name: Download React Build Artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: react-build
          path: app/build

      - name: Download Backend Artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: backend-zip
          path: .

      - name: Deploy to Production S3
        run: |
          aws s3 sync ./app/build s3://${{ env.FRONTEND_BUCKET }}/frontend/production/ --delete || true
          aws s3 cp backend.zip s3://${{ env.FRONTEND_BUCKET }}/backend/backend-prod.zip
```

## Assistant

**Yes, that's completely expected and correct behavior.**

### Why staging and production are being skipped:

Your workflow is currently set up like this (branch-driven):

- **Push to `development`** → only runs `Deploy to Development`
- **Push to `staging`** → only runs `Deploy to Staging`

how do I find my current ALB-DNS

## Assistant

**Here's the fastest and most reliable ways to find your current ALB DNS**, ranked from best to worst for your situation:

### 1. Best Option: Check Terraform Outputs (Recommended)

Since you're using Terraform, this is the cleanest way:

```bash
cd ~/aws-ha-autoscaling-project/terraform
terraform output alb_dns_name
```

This should print something like:
```
ha-project-alb-1234567890.us-east-1.elb.amazonaws.com
```

Then you would use it like this:
```
REACT_APP_API_BASE=http://ha-project-alb-1234567890.us-east-1.elb.amazonaws.com/api
```

---

### 2. Check Your GitHub Actions Logs (Very Easy)

Go to the **most recent successful "Deploy to Development"** run:

1. Go to your repo → **Actions**
2. Click on the latest green run on the `development` branch
3. Look inside the **"Deploy to Development"** job
4. Scroll through the logs — you should see a step that prints the ALB DNS (either from Terraform output or from the S3 upload step).

Many people also echo it during the deploy step. Search the logs for `elb.amazonaws.com`.

---

### 3. AWS Console (If you have any console access)

1. Go to **AWS Console → EC2**
2. In the left menu, click **Load Balancers**
3. Look for the load balancer named something like `ha-project-alb`
4. Click it → In the **Description** tab, copy the **DNS name**

It will look like: `ha-project-alb-XXXXXXXXXX.us-east-1.elb.amazonaws.com`

---

### 4. AWS CLI (Only if the others fail)

If your permissions allow it:

```bash
aws elbv2 describe-load-balancers \
  --query "LoadBalancers[?contains(LoadBalancerName, 'ha-project')].DNSName" \
  --output text
```

---

### What to do after you find it

Once you have the DNS, set it in GitHub like this:

**Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables**

Create a new Variable:
- **Name**: `REACT_APP_API_BASE`
- **Value**: `http://<your-alb-dns-here>/api`

Example:
```
http://ha-project-alb-1568483483.us-east-1.elb.amazonaws.com/api
```

### Root Cause
The user-data script that was baked into your current Launch Template version **only** sets up Apache for the frontend. It does **not** set up nginx as a reverse proxy, nor does it start your Node backend on port 3000. So when the ALB forwards `/api/*` requests, nothing is listening → 404.

I completely rewrote `terraform/modules/ec2/user-data.sh.tpl` with a proper bootstrap script that does the following on every new instance:

- Sets up Apache for the React frontend (from S3 `/frontend/current/`)
- Downloads and extracts your `backend.zip` from S3
- Sets up nginx as a reverse proxy (`/api/` → `http://127.0.0.1:3000`)
- Creates and starts a proper systemd service for the backend (`ha-backend`)
- Falls back to a minimal working server if the backend.zip is missing (so you at least stop getting 404s)

This is now the correct, complete user-data.

**Got it.** This is a common Git mistake — you're on the `development` branch and tried to push directly to `main`, but your local `main` is behind the remote `main`.

### What happened
- `git pull origin development` worked fine (your local dev branch was already up to date).
- `git push origin main` failed because the remote `main` branch has commits that your local `main` doesn't have (non-fast-forward).

---

### Correct way to promote from development → main

Since you want to go through the **production approval gate**, here's the safe sequence:

```bash
# 1. Switch to main and bring it up to date
git checkout main
git pull origin main

# 2. Merge your development work into main
git merge development

# 3. Push to main (this will trigger the production approval gate in your pipeline)
git push origin main
```

If there are any merge conflicts, Git will tell you — just resolve them, then run `git add .` + `git commit` + `git push` again.

---

### Important Notes

- Pushing to `main` will start the **"Approve Production Deployment"** job (the manual approval gate).
- If you actually wanted to go **development → staging first** (as you mentioned earlier), then do this instead:

```bash
git checkout staging
git pull origin staging
git merge development
git push origin staging
```

Then later merge `staging` into `main` when you're ready for the approval gate.

import React, { useState, useEffect, useCallback } from 'react';

const API_BASE = process.env.REACT_APP_API_BASE || 'http://ha-project-alb-1568483483.us-east-1.elb.amazonaws.com/api';

interface Todo {
  id: string;
  task: string;
  status?: string;
  priority?: string;
}

const TodoApp: React.FC = () => {
  const [user, setUser] = useState<any>(null);
  const [todos, setTodos] = useState<Todo[]>([]);
  const [newTodo, setNewTodo] = useState('');
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);
  const [apiError, setApiError] = useState<string | null>(null);

  const userId = user?.uid || 'demo-user-123';

  const fetchTodos = useCallback(async () => {
    try {
      setLoading(true);
      setApiError(null);
      const res = await fetch(`${API_BASE}/tasks?userId=${userId}`);
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`API error: ${res.status}`);
      const data = await res.json();
      setTodos(data.map((t: any) => ({
        id: t.id,
        task: t.task || t.title,
        status: t.status,
        priority: t.priority
      })));
    } catch (e) {
      console.error('Failed to fetch tasks', e);
      setApiError('Cannot reach backend. Tasks cannot be loaded or saved right now.');
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  }, [userId]);

  const addTodo = async () => {
    if (!newTodo.trim()) return;
    try {
      setApiError(null);
      const res = await fetch(`${API_BASE}/tasks`, {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify({ userId, title: newTodo.trim(), priority: 'Medium' })
      });
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`Failed to save: ${res.status}`);
      setNewTodo('');
      await fetchTodos();
    } catch (e) {
      console.error(e);
      setApiError('Failed to save task. Backend may be unreachable.');
    }
  };

  const toggleComplete = async (todo: Todo) => {
    const newStatus = todo.status === 'completed' ? 'pending' : 'completed';
    try {
      setApiError(null);
      const res = await fetch(`${API_BASE}/tasks/${todo.id}`, {
        method: 'PUT',
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify({ userId, status: newStatus })
      });
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`Update failed: ${res.status}`);
      await fetchTodos();
    } catch (e) {
      console.error(e);
      setApiError('Failed to update task. Backend may be unreachable.');
    }
  };

  useEffect(() => {
    const saved = localStorage.getItem('user');
    if (saved) setUser(JSON.parse(saved));
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (user) fetchTodos();
  }, [user, fetchTodos]);

  return (
    <div style={{
      minHeight: '100vh',
      background: 'linear-gradient(135deg, #f5f7fa 0%, #e4e8ec 100%)',
      padding: '40px 20px',
      fontFamily: 'system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif'
    }}>
      <div style={{ maxWidth: '680px', margin: '0 auto' }}>
        <h1 style={{ 
          fontSize: '42px', 
          fontWeight: 700, 
          textAlign: 'center', 
          marginBottom: '8px',
          color: '#1a1a1a'
        }}>
          To <span style={{ color: '#666', fontWeight: 400 }}>·</span> Do
        </h1>
        <p style={{ textAlign: 'center', color: '#666', marginBottom: '32px' }}>
          Persisted in MySQL RDS
        </p>

        {!user ? (
          <div style={{ textAlign: 'center' }}>
            <button 
              onClick={() => {
                const mock = { uid: 'demo-user-123', displayName: 'Demo User' };
                setUser(mock);
                localStorage.setItem('user', JSON.stringify(mock));
              }}
              style={{
                padding: '14px 32px',
                fontSize: 18,
                background: '#000',
                color: 'white',
                border: 'none',
                borderRadius: 8,
                cursor: 'pointer'
              }}
            >
              Sign in to start
            </button>
          </div>
        ) : (
          <div style={{
            background: 'white',
            borderRadius: 16,
            boxShadow: '0 10px 30px rgba(0,0,0,0.08)',
            padding: '32px'
          }}>
            <p style={{ marginBottom: 24, color: '#444' }}>
              Welcome, <strong>{user.displayName}</strong>
            </p>

            {apiError && (
              <div style={{
                background: '#fff3cd',
                color: '#856404',
                padding: '12px 16px',
                borderRadius: 8,
                marginBottom: 20,
                fontSize: 14
              }}>
                ⚠️ {apiError}
              </div>
            )}

            <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 12, marginBottom: 28 }}>
              <input
                value={newTodo}
                onChange={e => setNewTodo(e.target.value)}
                placeholder="What needs to be done?"
                style={{
                  flex: 1,
                  padding: '14px 18px',
                  fontSize: 16,
                  border: '1px solid #ddd',
                  borderRadius: 10,
                  outline: 'none'
                }}
                onKeyDown={e => e.key === 'Enter' && addTodo()}
              />
              <button 
                onClick={addTodo} 
                disabled={loading}
                style={{
                  padding: '14px 28px',
                  background: '#000',
                  color: 'white',
                  border: 'none',
                  borderRadius: 10,
                  fontSize: 15,
                  cursor: 'pointer'
                }}
              >
                Add
              </button>
            </div>

            {loading && <p style={{ color: '#888' }}>Loading...</p>}

            <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: 10 }}>
              {todos.length === 0 && !loading && (
                <p style={{ color: '#999', textAlign: 'center', padding: '20px 0' }}>
                  No tasks yet. Add one above!
                </p>
              )}

              {todos.map(todo => (
                <div 
                  key={todo.id}
                  style={{
                    display: 'flex',
                    alignItems: 'center',
                    gap: 14,
                    padding: '16px 20px',
                    background: '#fafafa',
                    borderRadius: 12,
                    border: '1px solid #eee'
                  }}
                >
                  <input
                    type="checkbox"
                    checked={todo.status === 'completed'}
                    onChange={() => toggleComplete(todo)}
                    style={{ width: 20, height: 20, cursor: 'pointer' }}
                  />
                  <span style={{ 
                    flex: 1, 
                    fontSize: 16,
                    textDecoration: todo.status === 'completed' ? 'line-through' : 'none',
                    color: todo.status === 'completed' ? '#888' : '#222'
                  }}>
                    {todo.task}
                  </span>
                  {todo.priority && (
                    <span style={{
                      fontSize: 12,
                      padding: '3px 10px',
                      background: '#f0f0f0',
                      borderRadius: 20,
                      color: '#555'
                    }}>
                      {todo.priority}
                    </span>
                  )}
                </div>
              ))}
            </div>

            <div style={{ marginTop: 32, textAlign: 'center' }}>
              <button 
                onClick={() => { localStorage.removeItem('user'); window.location.reload(); }}
                style={{ color: '#666', background: 'none', border: 'none', cursor: 'pointer' }}
              >
                Sign out
              </button>
            </div>
          </div>
        )}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
};

## Assistant

**Got it.** This is a common (and annoying) issue with ASG Instance Refresh.

### Why this is happening

AWS does **not** allow you to start a new Instance Refresh while one is still running on the same Auto Scaling Group. Your previous deployment triggered a refresh, and it's still in progress (or taking a long time), so the new one gets blocked.

The `|| echo "Refresh skipped"` in your workflow is already preventing the job from failing, which is good — but it also means **new code is not being picked up** on the instances until the previous refresh finishes.

This is likely why you're still seeing old behavior (or inconsistent results) even after a "successful" dev deployment.

---

### Recommended Fix

We should make this step smarter. The best approach for a **development** environment (where you deploy frequently) is:

- Check if a refresh is already running.
- If yes → **cancel the old one** first, then start a fresh one.

This way your latest code (new Launch Template + latest S3 assets) actually gets deployed quickly.

Here's the improved step you can replace in your workflow:

```yaml
      - name: Trigger ASG Refresh (pick up new code)
        run: |
          ASG_NAME="ha-project-asg"

          # Check for any in-progress refresh and cancel it (dev-friendly behavior)
          IN_PROGRESS=$(aws autoscaling describe-instance-refreshes \
            --auto-scaling-group-name $ASG_NAME \
            --query "InstanceRefreshes[?Status=='InProgress'].InstanceRefreshId" \
            --output text)

          if [ -n "$IN_PROGRESS" ]; then
            echo "Cancelling existing refresh: $IN_PROGRESS"
            aws autoscaling cancel-instance-refresh \
              --auto-scaling-group-name $ASG_NAME \
              --instance-refresh-id $IN_PROGRESS || true
            sleep 10
          fi

          echo "Starting new instance refresh..."
          aws autoscaling start-instance-refresh \
            --auto-scaling-group-name $ASG_NAME \
            --strategy Rolling \
            --preferences MinHealthyPercentage=0,InstanceWarmup=60 \
            --region ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
```

This version:
- Cancels any stuck/previous refresh (safe for dev)
- Uses more aggressive settings so new instances come up faster
- Still has the region from your env

---

### What to do next

1. Replace the "Trigger ASG Refresh" step in `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` with the improved version above.
2. Commit and push to `development`.
3. Manually trigger the "Deploy to Development" workflow.

## Assistant

**Got it.** You're stuck in a painful loop because the instances answering the ALB are still unhealthy or on old user-data.

I’m going to give you a **clean, simple, ultra-defensive** `user-data.sh.tpl` that prioritizes one thing above everything else:

**Never return 502 to the ALB.**  
It will always try to serve *something* (even a placeholder) and keep the health check happy.

### Step 1: Replace the entire file

Replace the **entire contents** of `terraform/modules/ec2/user-data.sh.tpl` with this:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set +e

# ULTRA DEFENSIVE - Goal: Never 502 the ALB
mkdir -p /var/www/html
cat > /var/www/html/index.html << 'HTMLEOF'
<!doctype html><html><body style="font-family:sans-serif;padding:2rem">
<h1>Instance is initializing...</h1>
<p>Please wait 1-2 minutes and refresh.</p>
</body></html>
HTMLEOF

echo "OK $(date -Iseconds)" > /var/www/html/health

# Minimal nginx that is almost impossible to break
cat > /etc/nginx/conf.d/ha-project.conf << 'NGINXEOF'
server {
    listen 80 default_server;
    server_name _;
    root /var/www/html;
    index index.html;

    location = /health {
        access_log off;
        return 200 "OK\n";
        add_header Content-Type text/plain;
    }

    location / {
        try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html;
    }
}
NGINXEOF

systemctl enable nginx 2>/dev/null || true
systemctl start nginx || systemctl restart nginx || true

# Now do the real work (best effort)
FRONTEND_BUCKET="${frontend_bucket}"
if aws s3 sync "s3://$FRONTEND_BUCKET/frontend/current/" /var/www/html/ --delete 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "Frontend synced"
fi

chown -R nginx:nginx /var/www/html 2>/dev/null || true
find /var/www/html -type d -exec chmod 755 {} + 2>/dev/null || true
find /var/www/html -type f -exec chmod 644 {} + 2>/dev/null || true

echo "OK $(date -Iseconds)" > /var/www/html/health

# Backend (optional - won't break the site if it fails)
mkdir -p /opt/ha-backend
if aws s3 cp "s3://$FRONTEND_BUCKET/backend/backend.zip" /tmp/backend.zip 2>/dev/null; then
  unzip -o /tmp/backend.zip -d /opt/ha-backend/ 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f /tmp/backend.zip
  cd /opt/ha-backend
  npm install --production 2>/dev/null || true
  cat > /etc/systemd/system/ha-backend.service << 'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Backend
After=network.target
[Service]
WorkingDirectory=/opt/ha-backend
ExecStart=/usr/bin/node server.js
Restart=always
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF
  systemctl daemon-reload
  systemctl enable ha-backend
  systemctl start ha-backend || true
fi

systemctl enable nginx
systemctl start nginx || systemctl restart nginx || true
```

Save the file.

**The exact issue right now is this:**

### The ALB has no healthy targets.

Your Application Load Balancer (`ha-project-alb-1568483483`) is returning **502 Bad Gateway** because **none of the EC2 instances it is currently sending traffic to are passing the health check**.

The health check is hitting `/health`. If that returns anything other than a quick 200, the ALB marks the instance unhealthy and stops sending traffic to it. When it has no healthy instances left, it returns 502 to the user.

This explains why:
- The whole site is 502 (not just the API)

        working-directory: ./terraform
